references.text: God commands Israel to build a sanctuary so that He may dwell among them, pointing to the promise of His presence in Exodus 29:43.
The glory of the Lord fills the tabernacle, fulfilling the promise that the sanctuary would be consecrated by God's glory.
God says He will show Himself holy among those who draw near to Him and will be glorified before all the people.
At the dedication of Solomon's temple, the cloud filled the Lord's house with His glory, just as God promised to do in the tabernacle.
Ezekiel sees the glory of the Lord fill the temple, reflecting the promise that God would sanctify the place with His glory.
Ezekiel sees the glory of the Lord fill the house of the Lord, a parallel to the promise of God's sanctifying presence.
The Word became flesh and dwelt among us, and we saw His glory – a fulfillment of God's promise to meet His people and reveal His glory.
Believers are the temple of the living God, and God will dwell among them, connecting to the promise of God's presence among the children of Israel.
Mutual illumination of how God is made holy among the people: through the presence of Glory and by avoiding desecration.
Ezekiel expands on the prophecy from Exodus that God's presence in the midst of His people is what makes them known and holy.
Highlights the continuity in God's plan to dwell among His people, from the tabernacle to the new covenant.
Direct fulfillment of the promise of God's presence: from the law in Exodus to the dedication of the temple in 1 Kings.
